description: Skill prerequisite dependency graph for engineering capstones

edges.description: Python is a prerequisite for PyTorch deep learning development
Python is a prerequisite for TensorFlow
Python is required for FastAPI asynchronous web backends
Python syntax is required for Pandas and NumPy
NumPy arrays and Pandas dataframes are required for Scikit-Learn pipelines
Classical ML concepts (loss, train/test split) precede deep neural networks
PyTorch model definition is exported to ONNX graph format
PyTorch tensors underpin HuggingFace transformers
Computer vision pipelines combine OpenCV preprocessing with PyTorch inference
Embedding vector spaces and distance metrics derive from ML feature vectors
Vector indexing powers Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for LLMs
HTTP and REST principles are required for FastAPI routing
Async/await coroutines power FastAPI endpoint performance
Relational query language is required for PostgreSQL schemas
TimescaleDB is an extension built directly on PostgreSQL
JavaScript syntax and runtime knowledge precedes TypeScript typing
TypeScript interfaces type React components and props
Complex React state flows necessitate Redux or Zustand slices
D3 and Recharts hook directly into React DOM and state lifecycle
C syntax, memory management, and pointers precede embedded microcontroller code
Embedded C firmware runs on ESP32 FreeRTOS microcontrollers
ESP32 GPIOs and hardware buses drive I2C/SPI sensors
Sensor readings are packaged and transmitted via MQTT telemetry
Microcontroller deployment target is required for TinyML execution
Model quantization and weight pruning precede microcontroller execution
Linux namespaces and cgroups form the architectural foundation of Docker
Container images are the atomic scheduling units for Kubernetes pods
Automated CI/CD pipelines build and verify Docker container images
Shell commands automate Linux system configuration and permissions
HTTP handshake initiates real-time WebSocket protocol upgrades
Single-node dataframes inform distributed dataset abstractions in Spark
